page: Amazon Web Services i8g.metal-24xl is a storage-optimized bare-metal server powered by 96 physical cores of the 64-bit ARM architecture. It features the AWS Neoverse-V2 processor running at 2.8 GHz with a dedicated core allocation and no hyperthreading. The hardware configuration includes 768.0 GB of DDR5 memory, providing 8.0 GB per core, and is bundled with 22,500 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. Network connectivity is supported by a 56 Gbps baseline bandwidth.

Benchmark data indicates top-tier multi-core performance, with stress-ng multi-core CPU and Geekbench multi-core scores placing in the top 10% of tested servers. The DDR5 memory subsystem delivers top-tier read and write bandwidth, reaching 481.52 GB/sec for large block reads and 218.23 GB/sec for large block writes. Database operations are highly efficient, as demonstrated by top-tier PassMark database operations and Redis SET operations processing at 197.01 million operations per second. However, single-core performance is more moderate, with stress-ng single-core and gzip single-threaded compression benchmarks landing in the average tier.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the server offers high resource density by combining massive local NVMe storage with a high-count ARM64 physical core layout, reducing the virtualization overhead typically associated with hyperthreaded environments. This makes it suitable for large-scale database deployments, high-throughput static web serving, and memory-intensive multi-threaded processing. It is less optimal for workloads reliant on single-threaded execution speeds or hardware-accelerated GPU tasks.

It is equipped with 768.0 GB of DDR5 memory and 22,500 GB of local NVMe SSD storage, supported by a 56 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Benchmarks show top-tier multi-core CPU performance, exceptional memory bandwidth, and high-efficiency database operations, including Redis SET operations at 197.01 million operations per second. Conversely, single-core benchmarks and single-threaded compression tasks perform in the average tier. Lacking a GPU, this server is designed for high-density storage and memory-intensive workloads. It is highly suited for large-scale databases, multi-threaded data processing, and high-throughput web serving where local NVMe storage and high physical core counts are required.
